name: Banh xeo
summary: Banh xeo is a crisp turmeric rice-flour crepe filled with pork and shrimp, eaten wrapped in herbs and lettuce with a dipping sauce. Central and southern versions differ in size.
origin: Southern and central Vietnam. Ho Chi Minh City is an easy place to eat a good one. In Da Nang the crepe runs smaller and crisper, and people wrap a piece in herbs before the dip. Can Tho counts a crispy pancake among its own plates. The Mekong version is large, filled with pork, bean sprouts, and shrimp, and eaten in a lettuce leaf with herbs and nước chấm.
howToEat: Break a piece, wrap it in a leaf with herbs, and dip. Do not eat it with a fork as a pancake.
It should be crisp when it lands. A soggy crepe has waited too long.
In the Mekong chapter the crepe is large, filled with pork, bean sprouts, and shrimp, and eaten in a lettuce leaf with herbs and nước chấm.

In Dong Hoi, roll the crepe with herbs, salad, and snakehead, then pinch it in bánh đa, just after it leaves the pan. Quảng Hòa soaks red rice about five hours and eats the crepe just off the pan with rau sống, nộm, cá chuối, and bánh đá.
where: In Da Nang the crepe is the smaller one on that city’s pages. Han Market and Con Market both turn it out from late morning.

In Hoi An, Vietnam Tourism says you slice the pancake and roll it with herbs and greens in dry rice paper, then dip. The Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 4 December 2025 article describes a small crisp crepe filled with shrimp, pork, and bean sprouts, rolled with herbs and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce.
In Can Tho, the crispy pancake is one of the city’s plates, and the Cồn Sơn garden kitchens make bánh xèo among their folk cakes.

In Ho Chi Minh City it is a crispy folded crepe with shrimp, pork, and bean sprouts, dipped in fish sauce, a southern-style savoury pancake. Sizzling bánh xèo is at the food stalls at the end of the Bến Thành hall.

The city serves two sizes. The Central pancake is small, less than a hand across, filled with green beans, bean sprouts, and some seafood or pork. The larger pancake is filled with shrimp, pork belly, bean sprouts, and green beans.

In Dong Hoi the crepe is red rice, with snakehead, a salad of bean sprouts, lettuce, and sesame, and bánh đa. Quảng Hòa uses the same red rice, with cá chuối and bánh đá. Bánh xèo Ba Đồn is a separate crepe.
priceBand: A shared plate plus herbs is a light meal.
seoDescription: How to eat banh xeo, wrapped in herbs, and where to order it.
